note: Winners of the ACM A.M. Turing Award in any field of computing, 1966 to 2025. Surname is enough. Alan Turing himself never won it

answers.q: ML the language, not that ML: he designed it in the 1970s. Also Hindley-Milner type inference. Turing Award 1991.
Backprop popularizer and Boltzmann machine co-inventor. Turing Award 2018, then the 2024 physics Nobel.
Convnets and LeNet. Shared the 2018 award with Hinton and Bengio.
Neural language models and attention, and the third of the 2018 deep learning trio.
The Art of Computer Programming. He sends a $2.56 check for each error found in his books.
Shortest paths, semaphores, and "Go To Statement Considered Harmful".
Bayesian networks and the do-calculus: the father of modern causal inference. Turing Award 2011.
TD learning, the RL textbook and The Bitter Lesson. Shared the 2024 award with Barto.
Published Perceptrons in 1969, the year he won. Co-founded MIT's AI Lab.
Coined "artificial intelligence" and invented Lisp. Turing Award 1971.
Logic Theorist and the General Problem Solver, with Herbert Simon.
Turing Award 1975 with Newell, and the 1978 Nobel in economics.
Created C and co-created Unix with Ken Thompson. They shared the 1983 award.
Unix, B, UTF-8 sketched on a diner placemat, and Go.
Quicksort, Hoare logic and the "billion-dollar mistake" of null references.
Logical clocks, Paxos and LaTeX. Turing Award 2013.
The R in RSA, and the designer of RC4 and MD5.
Invented the World Wide Web. Turing Award 2016.
Led the Fortran team and gave his name to Backus-Naur form.
Sutton's PhD adviser and co-author. Shared the 2024 award.
RISC and "Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach", then Google's TPU. Shared the 2017 award.
RISC pioneer who went on to be Stanford's president, then Alphabet's chair. Shared the 2017 award.
Co-designed TCP/IP with Robert Kahn. Turing Award 2004.
The Liskov substitution principle, and the CLU language. Turing Award 2008.
The Mythical Man-Month: adding people to a late project makes it later.
The relational model, 1970. SQL is its descendant.
The S in RSA, and the inventor of secret sharing.
The A in RSA. In 1994 he solved a Hamiltonian path problem with DNA in a test tube.
Public-key cryptography, 1976, with Hellman: "New Directions in Cryptography".
Diffie-Hellman key exchange. Turing Award 2015.
The Cook-Levin theorem: SAT is NP-complete.
Karp's 21 NP-complete problems, 1972. Also the Edmonds-Karp algorithm.
Strongly connected components, union-find analysis and splay trees.
Hopcroft-Karp matching and DFA minimization. Shared the 1986 award with Tarjan.
Pascal, Modula and Oberon. Wirth's law: software gets slower faster than hardware gets faster.
Smalltalk and the Dynabook idea. Turing Award 2003.
Co-designed TCP/IP with Vint Cerf. Turing Award 2004.
The 1968 "Mother of All Demos": mouse, hypertext and video conferencing.
Hamming codes and Hamming distance. Also the talk "You and Your Research".
Ingres, then Postgres: PostgreSQL descends from his Postgres.
LINPACK, BLAS and LAPACK, and a co-creator of the TOP500 supercomputer ranking.
Pixar co-founder. Texture mapping, the Z-buffer and Catmull-Clark subdivision surfaces.
Randomness and computation. Turing Award 2023, and the Abel Prize in 2021.
The father of expert systems: his group built DENDRAL.
PAC learning, 1984. Turing Award 2010.
Zero-knowledge proofs and probabilistic encryption, with Silvio Micali.
Zero-knowledge proofs and probabilistic encryption, with Shafi Goldwasser. Shared the 2012 award.
The Dragon Book on compilers, and the A in awk.
The Dragon Book with Aho, and the Mining of Massive Datasets textbook.
Yao's minimax principle and garbled circuits. Turing Award 2000.
Xerox PARC's Alto and Bravo, the first WYSIWYG editor.
The very first Turing Award, in 1966. Also the author of the Epigrams on Programming.
Built EDSAC in 1949 and invented microprogramming.
Backward error analysis in numerical linear algebra. A famously ill-conditioned polynomial carries his name.
Integrated Data Store, and the Turing lecture "The Programmer as Navigator".
Nondeterministic automata with Dana Scott, and the Miller-Rabin primality test.
Domain theory and denotational semantics. Shared the 1976 award with Michael Rabin.
Floyd-Warshall and Floyd-Steinberg dithering.
Invented APL. His Turing lecture was "Notation as a Tool of Thought".
An IBM RISC pioneer and a father of optimizing compilers.
Sketchpad in 1963, the ancestor of CAD and GUIs, then the first head-mounted display.
The father of IEEE 754 floating point, and the Kahan in Kahan summation.
CTSS and Multics, the time-sharing systems that gave computers passwords.
Founded computational complexity theory with Richard Stearns.
The time hierarchy theorem, with Juris Hartmanis.
Speech recognition pioneer at Carnegie Mellon. Shared the 1994 award with Feigenbaum.
Complexity axioms, and CAPTCHAs through his student Luis von Ahn.
Temporal logic for program verification.
Transaction processing and database recovery. He was lost at sea in 2007.
Simula, the first object-oriented language, with Kristen Nygaard.
Simula, the first object-oriented language, with Ole-Johan Dahl.
The N in Backus-Naur form, and editor of the Algol 60 report.
The first woman to win the Turing Award, for optimizing compilers.
Model checking, shared with Emerson and Sifakis in 2007.
Model checking, shared with Clarke and Sifakis in 2007.
Model checking, shared with Clarke and Emerson in 2007.
Chief designer of the Xerox Alto, the original personal computer.
RenderMan's shading language. Shared the 2019 award with Catmull.
Invented Ethernet and gave his name to Metcalfe's law.
BB84 quantum cryptography, with Brassard. Turing Award for 2025, announced in 2026.
BB84 and quantum teleportation, with Bennett. Turing Award for 2025.
